title: dedicated: improve autoscaler burst controls and fleet utilization reporting
author: Asha Patel
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky on first run, rerun)
release_notes: Improve Dedicated autoscaler burst accounting and introduce new utilization metrics; no breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets observed unexpected short-lived capacity spikes where burst allocations temporarily exceeded entitlements, causing downstream tail-latency regressions and opaque billing reports. This PR tightens burst controls, improves utilization reporting, and provides operators better tooling to reason about burst consumption.

What I changed (summary): - Introduced per-tenant burst token accounting and a soft cap enforcement path in the autoscaler. The new path prefers draining burst tokens before triggering preemptive scale-ups. - Added new telemetry metrics: dedicated_burst_allowed_tokens, dedicated_burst_used_tokens, dedicated_fleet_utilization_1m, dedicated_fleet_utilization_5m, and dedicated_fleet_utilization_1h for medium/long horizon reporting. These are exposed to Prometheus and surfaced in the Console. - Updated the throughput-guarantee logic so that guaranteed throughput is enforced independently of burst tokens; when guarantees are at risk we trigger prioritized scale-ups. - Added a CLI helper (cmd/ops/burstctl) to simulate and inspect burst allocations on a fleet for debugging. - E2E tests to validate burst capping behavior and utilization report generation under synthetic load. - Docs: expanded docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md with examples and recommended knob values.

Why: Teams running latency-sensitive workloads need predictable tail latency and transparent billing. By separating burst accounting from throughput guarantees and exposing multi-horizon utilization metrics we can both limit unbounded bursts and give SREs a clearer signal to act on.

Checklist: - [x] Add per-tenant burst accounting in autoscaler. - [x] Expose and document new metrics. - [x] Add CLI tooling for ops. - [x] Add unit & e2e tests. - [x] Update docs and release notes.

Notes on behaviour changes: The autoscaler's default burst policy is unchanged for existing clusters. New clusters and those that enable the tighter enforcement flag will apply the soft cap; operators can opt-in to hard caps after monitoring for one week.

Related: ENG-4213 tracks the wider throughput-guarantee work; SUP-1342 was a customer case that motivated better reporting.
